comments.author: ptimizeroracle
comments.body:
I went through both sides of this with the current code (main @ 99b9109). Happy to turn any of it into a fix if wanted, but evidence first.

**The two numbers are different estimators, not two measurements of the same thing:**

| | bench_serving | engine log |
|---|---|---|
| definition | TPOT-derived, per request: `(latency − ttft)` over `output_len − 1`, averaged across the whole run, client-side | `num_generated_tokens / gap_latency` where `gap_latency` is the time since the previous log line (`scheduler_components/metrics_reporter.py:799,894`) |
| window | entire run: queueing, any cold start, `[DONE]` tail included | one reporting interval, near-instantaneous |

So bench < engine is expected whenever the run has any ramp-up: the engine line reads close to a short-window peak, the bench number is a whole-run average.

Three smaller things verified along the way (all `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py` unless noted):

1. TPOT arithmetic is the standard upstream vLLM formula (`(latency − ttft)/(output_len − 1)`, `:1136`): sound.
2. `itl` is recorded per stream **event**, not per token (`:334-337`, `:466+`). Events carrying several tokens (stream-interval batching, speculative decoding) contribute one itl sample, so `len(itl) < output_len − 1` and ITL percentiles conflate event latency with token latency. A retokenized correction already exists, but only for the `sglang-oai` backends (`:1131-1135`, `:1145-1155`); the completions/chat paths don't get it. I wrote CPU unit tests pinning this behavior (sum(itl) + [DONE]-tail == latency − ttft exactly; mean(ITL) > TPOT for the same request from denominators alone). Happy to PR them.
3. `should_flush_cache` is `("sglang" in backend AND SGLANG_IS_IN_CI) or --flush-cache` (`:1467-1471`), not default-on, so the cold-start mechanism discussed earlier in this thread needs CI or the explicit flag to apply to a default run.

If it's useful, the options I see: (a) a note in the bench output clarifying the window difference vs engine logs, (b) an engine-side long-window average for apples-to-apples runs, (c) extending the retokenized ITL path to the other backends. Which, if any, would you want?

shortlist.title: bug: a client-set `X-Conversation-Id` disables disconnect-cancellation and accumulates uncapped resumable-stream sessions, can cause memory DoS
shortlist.author: Yunzez
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

`llama-server`, git `4b1a27f` (`version: 0.5.0-dev (build 1)`), CPU build, Linux x86_64, `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf`. No special launch flag (the resumable-stream manager starts unconditionally at boot).


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8137 -c 2048 -np 1 --no-webui python3 repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8137
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Repro script: [repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/f99b245d040ac2604178c1bef9541d6b#file-repro_llamacpp_stream_session_dos-py)

The resumable-stream session manager keys a per-request session on the **client-controlled** `X-Conversation-Id` header. When that header is present, two things go wrong, both exploitable by an unauthenticated client:

**(A) A socket disconnect no longer cancels the generation.** With `X-Conversation-Id`, `server_res_spipe::should_stop()` (`tools/server/server-stream.cpp:622-628`) returns `spipe->is_cancelled()`, which is set only by an explicit `DELETE /v1/stream` — instead of `!conn_alive()`. So a streaming request whose client hangs up keeps the inference slot busy generating to its natural stop. An attacker fires `stream:true` requests with a large `max_tokens` and drops each connection immediately; every abandoned request still consumes a full generation and pins a slot. 

Measured on a single-slot server (`-np 1`): after abandoning one stream, a normal follow-up request was blocked **36.9 s** (the whole generation) with the header, versus **0.07 s** without it (disconnect cancels normally).

**(B) Sessions accumulate with no cap and a 300 s post-completion TTL.** Each session buffers up to `STREAM_SESSION_MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB` of SSE output (`server-stream.cpp:18`) and is retained for `STREAM_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 300 s` **after** the generation completes before the GC removes it (`gc_loop`, `server-stream.cpp:356`). `create_or_replace` (`:235`) just `emplace`s into an `unordered_map,  **there is no cap on the number of sessions**. A client that sends streaming requests with a fresh `X Conversation-Id` each time and never issues `DELETE /v1/stream` accumulates ~`rate × 300 s` sessions, each holding up to 4 MiB, eventually will cause memory exhaustion.

Ablation confirms the header is the cause: 150 streaming requests **without** the header grow `VmHWM` by ~0 MB (sessions are evicted on completion — `on_complete` at `server-stream.cpp:638`), while 150 **with** unique headers retain their sessions (monotonic growth; at large `max_tokens` each retains up to 4 MiB).

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

```console

```
</details>

<!-- Long logs that you upload as files go here, outside the "console" area -->

comments.author: benthecarman
comments.body:
A related problem: sessions live in one global map (`g_stream_sessions`, `server-stream.cpp:65`), keyed only by the client-supplied `X-Conversation-Id`. Nothing ties a session to the caller's API key. So anyone who knows or guesses another client's ID can:

- read that client's buffered output: `GET /v1/stream` (`:454`)
- cancel their generation: `DELETE /v1/stream` (`:561`)
- replace their session by sending their own request with the same ID; `create_or_replace` cancels the existing session (`:235-255`)

Also, a `DELETE` with an unknown ID writes every live conversation ID to the log at WARN (`:297-304`).

This only matters when several clients share one server and IDs aren't random (the web UI uses UUIDs). One possible fix is to scope sessions to the API key that created them, and to stop logging live IDs.

## Status

Draft / implementation in review.

This RFC replaces the oversized prototype PR #2896 with six smaller draft PRs that have an explicit review and merge topology.

## Motivation

Several Mooncake Store unit-test executables contain many semantically unrelated cases and run for a long time as one scheduling unit. Splitting those cases by behavior gives CTest more useful parallel work and makes failures easier to locate, but creating one executable per source file increases compile/link overhead.

The proposal therefore separates two concerns:

1. Keep source files organized by semantic behavior.
2. Use a small CMake helper to combine compatible files into a bounded number of Unity-built test targets.

No hard-coded shard index or test-name routing table is introduced.

## Invariants

- Preserve all 296 source-defined GTest cases.
- Changes to test-only fixture behavior are acceptable when needed for isolation.
- Production behavior must not change.
- Each domain split must remain independently reviewable.
- The final target-balancing change must be isolated in its own commit/PR layer.

## PR topology

```text
                         +--> #2900 DummyClient + offload --------+
                         +--> #2901 SSD + snapshot SSD -----------+
RFC #2898 / main --------+--> #2902 promotion --------------------+--> #2905 Unity/target balance
                         +--> #2903 MasterService core -----------+
                         +--> #2904 snapshot MasterService -------+
```

The five domain PRs are all based directly on the same `main` commit and can be reviewed in parallel. #2905 contains those five commits plus one final CMake-only commit; review that final commit after the domain PRs, then let its diff shrink as #2900–#2904 merge.

## Tracking

| Order | PR | Scope | Source tests | Review dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | #2900 | DummyClient + offload | 17 | RFC only |
| 2 | #2901 | SSD + snapshot SSD | 26 | RFC only |
| 3 | #2902 | Promotion | 40 | RFC only |
| 4 | #2903 | MasterService core | 144 | RFC only |
| 5 | #2904 | Snapshot MasterService | 69 | RFC only |
| 6 | #2905 | Unity build and target balancing | 296 total | #2900–#2904 |

## CMake design

`add_store_test()` remains the single registration primitive. The final PR adds `add_store_unity_test()`, which delegates to it and enables CMake `UNITY_BUILD` for compatible semantic source groups.

The result is:

- 30 independently registered targets in the five domain PRs, useful for isolated review and validation.
- 21 balanced targets in the final integrated layout.
- Semantic directories and filenames remain intact.
- No numeric shard constants or hard-coded test-case mapping in CMake.

## Validation

Five independent branches:

- All targeted builds passed.
- 30/30 CTest targets passed.
- Source-defined test count: 17 + 26 + 40 + 144 + 69 = 296.
- Four-way group wall times: 32.69s, 43.32s, 36.63s, 85.97s, and 89.85s.

Final integration branch:

- 21/21 targets built on current `main`.
- 21/21 CTest targets passed with `ctest -j4` in 204.53s.
- Isolated prototype measurement: 148.05s target build and 203.81s test time.
- A contended cold build measured 490.52s after four concurrent worktree builds; it is retained as a host-load datapoint and is not used as a regression comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] 296 source-defined tests preserved.
- [x] Semantic source layout replaces the long monoliths.
- [x] Final test wall time is at most 210s at four-way concurrency.
- [x] Isolated changed-target build is at most 160s.
- [x] Combined isolated build + test time is at most 360s.
- [x] Domain PRs can be reviewed in parallel.
- [x] Target balancing is isolated for focused review.

## Rollout

1. Review #2900–#2904 in parallel.
2. Merge accepted domain PRs in any order, resolving only localized CMake registration overlap if needed.
3. Rebase #2905 as those PRs land.
4. Review the final CMake-only target-balancing commit.
5. Mark the drafts ready only after human review of every changed line and successful CI.

## Superseded prototype

#2896 demonstrated the full approach but is too large to review effectively. It is superseded by this RFC and #2900–#2905.

shortlist.title: [good-first-issue] tests: stabilize flaky CI tests from recent PRs
shortlist.author: maobaolong
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Part of #3372. This is a community tracker for small, independently claimable improvements to flaky tests.

## The problem

Recent PR CI contains assertions that race background work and an intermittent hang that can occupy a runner for almost six hours. These failures consume contributor time and make unrelated PRs harder to validate.

The initial triage reviewed GitHub Actions `Test` runs from September 13-23, 2026 and recent `k3-unit-tests` failures. These are selected examples, not a complete inventory or a measured repository-wide flake rate. The test code was checked against `dev` at [21571dae80c6](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/commit/21571dae80c64ab4d141be571744494995270160).

The initial tasks cover:

- **Health-monitor exit:** a fixed 200 ms sleep precedes a thread-exit assertion; two PRs have same-checkout failed/passed attempts.
- **Health-monitor fallback/recovery:** a fixed 200 ms sleep precedes a state assertion; failure logs show fallback completing after the assertion.
- **RESP wait diagnostics:** a same-checkout rerun passes after an almost-six-hour hang near the RESP test boundary. The exact blocked operation remains unproven; this task adds bounded waits and diagnostics, not a speculative production fix.

## Initial tasks

- [x] #5314: Synchronize health-monitor exception-driven exit
- [ ] #5315: Synchronize health-monitor fallback/recovery phases
- [ ] #5316: Bound RESP waits and add stalled-operation diagnostics

## September 22–29 follow-up tasks

The follow-up scan covered **September 22, 2026 04:31 UTC through September 29, 2026 04:31 UTC**. It inspected 1,338 GitHub Actions run records across `Test`, `CPU Device Tests`, and `Operator: CI`, and 2,106 Buildkite build records across the active LMCache pipelines, then examined relevant failed jobs and retry logs. These inventory counts are not a repository-wide flake rate or a claim that every failed log was exhaustively analyzed.

Each new task below includes a failed/passed pair within the **same `dev` Buildkite build**, with the same LMCache checkout and vLLM/torch versions. PR-head-only matches with an unverified base merge, dependency/version changes between attempts, and one-off failures were not used as confirmation.

- [ ] #5402: Make `vllm_bench` inputs reproducible across retries and retain the comparison settings/results. Build #5340 changes from 7.34% slower than baseline to 0.62% faster without a source change.
- [ ] #5403: Preserve separate baseline/LMCache raw timings for `long_doc_qa`. Build #5294 changes from 50.3% TTFT improvement (fail) to 70.4% (pass); #5291 provides a second pair.
- [ ] #5404: Retain L2 data-flow diagnostics after `long_doc_qa_l2` performance failures. Build #5287 changes from 1.49x TTFT speedup (fail) to 1.54x (pass).

These are independently claimable **reproducibility and diagnostics improvements for confirmed intermittent test verdicts**. They deliberately keep the existing performance/data-flow assertions. Completing a diagnostic task does not establish that the underlying timing instability is fixed; report any remaining root-cause work separately.

Contributors can develop the scoped regression coverage with CPU-only command stubs. End-to-end validation uses two CUDA GPUs and the exact CI workload; each child provides a self-contained historical reproduction recipe. A maintainer can help with GPU validation. The CPU environment below applies to the initial #5314–#5316 tasks, not these GPU workload runs.

Existing health-monitor/RESP tasks and ongoing MQ, distributed-storage, and observability work were checked to avoid duplicate newcomer assignments. Intermittent model-output mismatches were not turned into generic timing-hardening tasks or described as harmless flakes.

## Claim one sub-issue

Use the native **Sub-issues** list below. Start with either health-monitor task if this is your first test contribution; the RESP task benefits from familiarity with Python futures and event loops.

These tasks are primarily meant to help new contributors learn the LMCache contribution workflow. Please claim **only one sub-issue at a time**. If you already have an assigned task or an open PR in this tracker, finish that one before taking another, and leave the remaining tasks for other new contributors.

1. Pick one unassigned sub-issue and check its comments for an existing claim.
2. Comment `/claim` or "I'd like to work on this" **on that sub-issue**, so a maintainer can coordinate assignment. Please do not claim the parent tracker itself.
3. Keep one task per PR, target `dev`, and follow [the onboarding guide](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/3372) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md).
4. Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`), run `pre-commit run --all-files`, and include exact test commands and results in the PR.

## Shared CPU test setup (initial tasks)

The initial #5314–#5316 tasks do not require a GPU, model download, or external Redis server. Use Linux x86_64 with Git, a C/C++ build toolchain, FFmpeg, and Python 3.12 with venv support. The RESP tests use an in-memory mocked client. Allow sufficient disk space for PyTorch/vLLM dependencies. The full pre-commit checks also need Rust/Cargo with rustfmt and clippy.

Run this in a fresh working directory. The explicit revision is the **triage reference**; make the actual PR against current `dev`.

shortlist.title: Refactor: TRTLLMHAAttnBackend should not inherit from FlashInferAttnBackend when reuse is small
shortlist.author: merrymercy
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Summary

`TRTLLMHAAttnBackend(FlashInferAttnBackend)` (in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/trtllm_mha_backend.py`) inherits from `FlashInferAttnBackend`, but it reuses very little from the parent. Almost all attention-specific behavior is overridden, and some inherited setup is allocated-but-never-used. We should reconsider this inheritance: **if the reuse is small, we should not inherit from `FlashInferAttnBackend`** — inheriting directly from the base `AttentionBackend` (and pulling in only the small bits of plumbing that are actually shared) would be cleaner.

### What is actually reused

The only real reuse comes from `super().__init__(...)`:
- `req_to_token_pool`, `token_to_kv_pool`
- `max_context_len`, `skip_prefill`, `use_sliding_window_kv_pool`
- the `kv_indptr` / `kv_last_page_len` buffers (used by the companion `TRTLLMHAAttnMultiStepDraftBackend` draft steps)
- `forward()` dispatch — which actually comes from the base `AttentionBackend`, not from FlashInfer.

### What is overridden (not reused)

Essentially all the attention logic:
- `init_forward_metadata`, `init_cuda_graph_state`, `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`
- `forward_decode`, `forward_extend` (call `flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` / `flashinfer.prefill.trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` directly)
- `get_cuda_graph_seq_len_fill_value`, `_resolve_swa_kv_pool`
- it uses its own `TRTLLMMHAMetadata` and its own page-table builder.

### Inherited-but-unused / redundant work

Because the TRTLLM kernels use a completely different API, part of the parent `__init__` is wasted:
- Parent builds `prefill_wrapper_ragged`, `prefill_wrappers_paged`, `decode_wrappers`, and the `FlashInferIndicesUpdater*` objects — TRTLLM-MHA never uses them.
- Parent sets `self.workspace_buffer` to the shared `global_workspace_buffer`, but the child **replaces** it with its own zero-init `global_zero_init_workspace_buffer`.
- `max_context_len` and `_swa_kv_pool` are set by the parent and then re-set by the child.

### Proposal

- Evaluate inheriting `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` directly from `AttentionBackend` instead of `FlashInferAttnBackend`.
- Move the small amount of genuinely shared init plumbing into a thin shared helper/mixin (e.g. pool/buffer setup) rather than dragging in the full FlashInfer wrapper/indices-updater allocation.
- Avoid allocating FlashInfer wrappers and updaters that the TRTLLM path never uses.
- Apply the same review to `TRTLLMHAAttnMultiStepDraftBackend(FlashInferMultiStepDraftBackend)`.

As a general guideline: **do not inherit from `FlashInferAttnBackend` when the reuse is little** — prefer inheriting from the base `AttentionBackend` and sharing only what is actually common.

### Good first issue

This is a good first issue: it is well-scoped, localized to `trtllm_mha_backend.py` (plus the base classes), and mostly a refactor with clear before/after behavior to validate against existing tests.

shortlist.title: llama-quantize: GGML_ASSERT(size mismatch) when quantizing mmproj files containing 3D conv tensors (gemma4v audio conv1d)
shortlist.author: mrBenBern
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Quantizing the gemma-4-E2B combined mmproj (vision+audio, gemma4v/gemma4a projectors) from F16 to Q8_0 aborts with:

  llama-quant.cpp:1365: GGML_ASSERT(gguf_get_tensor_size(...) == new_size) failed

Repro:
  llama-quantize --allow-requantize mmproj-F16.gguf out.gguf Q8_0

Fails at tensor `a.conv1d.0.weight` — shape [3,3,1,128] (3D conv1d from the audio encoder). The f32→f16 conversion changes the tensor size, and the split-output writer asserts on the mismatch. Every subsequent 3D tensor fails the same way (a.conv1d.1.weight [3,3,128,32], ...).

Workaround (verified): keep 3D tensors in f32 via tensor-type overrides —
  llama-quantize --allow-requantize \
    --tensor-type "a.conv1d.0.weight=f32" \
    --tensor-type "a.conv1d.1.weight=f32" \
    mmproj-F16.gguf mmproj-F16-q8_0.gguf Q8_0

This works and the resulting Q8_0 mmproj is functionally correct on-device (Android, llama.cpp 4ebdf2c): vision outputs verified same-in-quality as F16 (sign-text reading), encode on a Helio G99 CPU improved 6.4x vs BF16 (37s -> 5.8s for a 91-token image).

Expected behavior: either skip/conversion-preserving handling for N-D tensors whose element count doesn't allow requantization, or a clean error message listing the offending tensors instead of an assert.

shortlist.title: Performance comparison for dense shared prefix + block-diagonal local mask: custom mask in BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper vs MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper
shortlist.author: catnanami
shortlist.body_excerpt: I am trying to evaluate the best way to implement an attention pattern with a dense shared/global prefix plus a local block-diagonal suffix. The mask pattern is shown below: I am considering two implementations: BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper with a custom mask MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper Questions: 1. For this pattern, is cascade attention expected to be faster than paged prefill with a custom mask? 2. Or is this pattern better handled by a custom kernel/backend? My use case is speculative decoding, where all verification tokens share the same prefix KV, but each local block should only attend to its own block.

comments.author: VectorPeak
comments.body:
For the mask in the image - a dense shared prefix on the left plus independent block-diagonal local regions on the right - `MultiLevelCascadeAttentionWrapper` is usually the better fit than `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` with one large custom mask.

The reason is that the custom-mask prefill path does not really exploit this structure as well: it still treats the problem like one masked attention problem over the full layout, so the block-diagonal sparsity mostly becomes masking overhead. Cascade attention lets you model this as:

- shared/global prefix KV: attended by all verification tokens
- local suffix KV: split into independent blocks/requests
- final result: merge prefix-attention state with each local block’s attention state

For speculative decoding, this is exactly the kind of case where cascade can help, especially when the shared prefix is large and the local verification blocks are relatively small. Each local block can be represented as a separate batch item sharing the same prefix. If the local part also needs causal masking inside each block, use the normal causal/local mask for that per-block suffix attention.

shortlist.title: [good-first-issue] tests: retain L2 diagnostics when flaky TTFT checks fail
shortlist.author: maobaolong
shortlist.body_excerpt:
Parent tracker: #5313 · Onboarding: #3372

## Confirmed flaky behavior

`k3-multiprocess-test / vllm / long_doc_qa_l2 / zmq` changes its L2 time-to-first-token (TTFT) verdict on a same-source retry:

| Build #5287, September 26, 2026 (UTC) | Query speedup | TTFT speedup | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Original job](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5287#01a0db08-cd08-4819-aafd-3b1599eed368) | 1.46x | **1.49x** | Fails the 1.5x TTFT requirement |
| [Retry](https://buildkite.com/lmcache/k3-multiprocess-test/builds/5287#01a0db28-e4d4-4a86-96f8-6923e870be90) | 1.43x | **1.54x** | Passes |

Both jobs test `dev` commit **`002693d8aa5ba8ead0d67922540e4ad4ba6fb3d3`**, without a PR-base merge, and install vLLM **`0.30.1rc1.dev142+g3a58aeb1a`** and torch **`2.13.0+cu130`**. The retry additionally reports 1190 successful L2 stores, 95 prefetch lookups, 2340 prefix hits, and 2340 loaded keys.

The failed attempt exits before the L2 data-flow checks, so we cannot tell from those checks whether it exercised the same successful cache path. That diagnostic gap must not be treated as evidence of broken L2 retrieval, or as proof that the fluctuation is harmless noise.

## Bounded good-first task

Ensure a performance-threshold failure still captures and checks L2 data-flow evidence before the workload exits.

In `long-doc-qa-l2.sh`, `set -e` is active. Step 3's Python threshold verifier exits nonzero, so Step 4's Prometheus scrape and L2 store/prefetch validation never run on the failing path. This is a small shell control-flow and test-diagnostics task.

1. Retain the performance verification status instead of immediately exiting. Run the existing bounded metrics collection while the L2 server is still alive.
2. Report **both** performance and data-flow outcomes, save the metrics snapshot, then return failure if either outcome fails. A metrics timeout/missing snapshot must remain visible and must not mask the original performance failure.
3. Make the snapshot and summary accessible in the public job log or a job artifact. Keep the change local to the L2 workload and any narrowly needed artifact rule.
4. Add CPU-only coverage with stubbed verifier/scrape commands for: both pass, only performance fails, only metrics/data-flow fails, and both fail. Assert bounded behavior, metrics collection after a performance failure, and the final exit status.

Keep the existing 1.3x query-speedup, 1.5x TTFT-speedup, 1.2x warmup-overhead limits and positive L2 data-flow assertions. Do not add blanket retries, reduce thresholds, or redesign storage policy. This completes the missing diagnostics for a confirmed flake; it does **not** by itself establish that the GPU timing instability is fixed. Keep the L1 wrapper outside this task.

Starting points, checked at `42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052`:

- [L2 workload: threshold verifier followed by metrics checks](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/workloads/common/long-doc-qa-l2.sh#L229).
- [Result cleanup/copying](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/scripts/cleanup.sh).
- [Buildkite workload step](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/42be9c7439a1eb0b17bf6b7565a894a9743fd052/.buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/pipeline.yml#L173).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A forced performance failure still collects bounded L2 diagnostics before cleanup.
- [ ] All four outcome combinations have regression coverage and correct final exit status.
- [ ] A failed GPU comparison exposes the available store/prefetch counters, or an explicit collection error, in public output/artifacts.
- [ ] Existing thresholds and data-flow assertions remain effective.
- [ ] The PR reports remaining timing instability separately from completed diagnostic hardening.

## Reproduce the CI workload

The evidence below comes from CI; this issue does not claim a local GPU reproduction. Use a dedicated Linux x86_64 GPU test host with Docker and NVIDIA Container Toolkit, two available CUDA GPUs capable of running separate `Qwen/Qwen3-14B` servers, sufficient host RAM for the default 80 GiB LMCache buffer (plus the mock L2 storage for the L2 case), and disk/network access for the image, wheels, and model. CI uses CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12, and a 1 GiB `/dev/shm`. A maintainer can run the GPU validation for a contributor who only has a CPU machine.

These commands build the public CI image recipe, explicitly start Bash, and pin the historical LMCache and vLLM revisions. They are a reproduction recipe, not a fully locked copy of every historical dependency or GPU scheduling condition. Run from a fresh directory; make the actual PR against current `dev`.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache.git
cd LMCache
git checkout 002693d8aa5ba8ead0d67922540e4ad4ba6fb3d3
docker build -t lmcache-flake-ci \
  -f .buildkite/k3_harness/ci-base.Dockerfile .
docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0,1"' --shm-size=1g \
  --entrypoint bash \
  -v "$PWD:/workspace/LMCache" -w /workspace/LMCache \
  -e MAX_JOBS=1 \
  -e INFERENCE_ENGINE=vllm \
  -e LMCACHE_REQUEST_TRANSPORT=zmq \
  -e LMCACHE_PR_BASE_MERGE=never \
  -e PINNED_VLLM_VERSION=0.30.1rc1.dev142+g3a58aeb1a \
  -e PINNED_VLLM_ARCHIVE_INDEX_URL=https://wheels.vllm.ai/3a58aeb1a13e7447da3037608d6489da7e7f22a2/cu130 \
  lmcache-flake-ci -c '
    set -e
    source /opt/venv/bin/activate
    command -v git uv python3 nvcc gcc g++
    nvidia-smi
    git config --global --add safe.directory /workspace/LMCache
    .buildkite/k3_tests/multiprocess/run.sh long_doc_qa_l2
  '
```

Use the linked failed and passed jobs as the initial reproduction pair. For subsequent GPU runs, record the actual checkout SHA, installed package versions, GPU model, input settings, and first-attempt result. A green retry alone does not show that the underlying fluctuation was fixed.

shortlist.title: [RFC]: Support SparDA-style decoupled Forecast projection for lookahead KV prefetch in sparse attention
shortlist.author: Srinivasoo7
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Motivation.

This RFC frames the two problems (PCIe bottleneck on offloaded KV, O(T²) selection cost), introduces SparDA's Forecast projection as the fix, cites the paper's reported speedups.

### Proposed Change.

(1) new Forecast projection in the model definition, one per GQA group, 
(2) lookahead block selection at layer N for layer N+1, 
(3) prefetch fired through the existing KVConnector path one layer early.

### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@orozery 

### Any Other Things.

Feasibility:
This points to the DSA/lightning-indexer integration as proof that the attention-backend abstraction supports extra selector projections, and to the existing KVConnector async offload path plus RFC #38260 as the infra this would extend, not duplicate.

Open questions:
Whether the connector can be triggered a layer early today, where the Forecast projection should live architecturally, whether to build a generic lookahead-selector abstraction, and how to gate on checkpoint/model availability.


Related References:
https://github.com/NVlabs/SparDA
Related RFCs: #38260,  #19854

comments.author: catyans
comments.body:
Deterministic shadow-scheduler experiment (2026-07-13) to test the core enforcement hypothesis before touching Admission. This is simulation evidence only.

Environment: Lingjun H20 `lingjun-099`, Python 3.12.7 / NumPy, fixed seed 20260713. Model: 10,000 x 1 ms epochs, capacity 100 work units/epoch; foreground arrivals Poisson(40/epoch), background Poisson(90/epoch), foreground deadline 5 epochs. Compared a single unbiased FIFO against a work-conserving 60/40 class budget; unused foreground capacity was borrowed by background.

Results:

| mode | FG completed / arrived | FG miss | FG P99 wait | BG completed | utilization | final FG/BG backlog |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FIFO | 307,991 / 400,150 | 99.829% | 2,286 epochs | 692,009 | 100% | 92,159 / 207,355 |
| budget | 400,150 / 400,150 | 0.000% | 0 epochs | 599,850 | 100% | 0 / 299,514 |

Conclusion: under sustained aggregate overload, explicit class budgets can protect feasible foreground demand while remaining work-conserving; the benefit is not higher total throughput (both are 100% utilized), but controlled allocation. The cost is explicit: background service fell by 92,159 units and its backlog grew, so aging/reclaim and overload policy are mandatory. This does not validate real TENT timing, hierarchical identity, byte-vs-request accounting or distributed guarantees. A code PR should begin in shadow-accounting mode and reproduce this comparison with tebench and real RDMA before enforcement is enabled.

shortlist.title: [Misc]: CMake Clean-up / Refactor Tasks
shortlist.author: LucasWilkinson
shortlist.body_excerpt:
In an effort to make the CMake more readable, stable and easy to use we have a few tasks we'd like to work on, creating a GitHub issue here to track that progress, some planned changes/investigations:

- [ ] Rename `define_gpu_extension_target`, currently this is used for CPU extensions too so the name is now misleading
- [ ] Add a CI test of local builds, i.e. `pip install -e .`
- [ ]  Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8845), currently if there is a `+PTX` in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` this will be ignored. We should warn when this is the case. Alternatively we can add support for PTX builds although this is generally not desirable since PTX increases the wheel size by quite a bit (PTX is larger than SASS), and we already build for all currently supported arches.
- [ ]  Have vllm-flash-attn use [ExternalProject](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/ExternalProject.html) currently vllm-flash-attn uses the parent CMake scope which creates many footguns since it is in a separate repo, using `ExternalProject` will mean that the vllm-flash-attn will be run in a separate CMake scope/process
  - [ ] It might be even better to revert to the FlashMLA approach, where CMake code lives in vllm.
- [ ] Look into removing early returns in CMakeLists.txt (potentially move backends into its own files)
- [ ] Potential build both C++ and CUDA extensions when building for CUDA and using torch dispatcher to dispatch between the two, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8424

@ProExpertProg @LucasWilkinson 

Hey! I noticed the first item (renaming `define_gpu_extension_target`) was completed in #28026, so I'd like to take a crack at the next one - adding a CI test for local builds (`pip install -e .`).

**My understanding**: Right now the CI tests run against pre-built Docker images, so if someone accidentally breaks the build system (CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, csrc/), the tests still pass and we only find out when the Docker image build fails separately. This test would catch that earlier by actually building from source.

Based on the current CI setup (CPU-only tests in GitHub Actions, GPU/specialized hardware in Buildkite), I'm thinking this should go in Buildkite since the main goal is testing CUDA and AMD/ROCm builds. The macOS smoke test in GitHub Actions already covers the CPU build path.

**A couple of questions:**

1. How thorough should it be? Just verify the build succeeds, or also run a quick inference smoke test like the macOS workflow does?

2. Should it run on every PR, or only when build-related files change? I'm thinking we could use `source_file_dependencies` to trigger only on changes to CMakeLists.txt, cmake/*, csrc/*, setup.py, etc.

Happy to adjust based on what makes sense. Thanks!

shortlist.title: [Gluon] async_load accepts a pointer whose element type differs from the shared memory buffer
shortlist.author: shuyilinn
shortlist.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Gluon's `async_copy.async_load` (and `async_copy_global_to_local` in general) does not check that the pointer element type matches the shared memory element type. Copying from an fp32 pointer into an fp16 buffer compiles and copies raw bytes, and the reverse faults with a misaligned address. `smem.store` rejects the same mismatch at compile time.

```python
import torch
from triton.experimental import gluon
from triton.experimental.gluon import language as gl
from triton.experimental.gluon.language.nvidia.ampere import async_copy


@gluon.jit
def kernel(inp, out, SMEM_DTYPE: gl.constexpr, N: gl.constexpr):
    L: gl.constexpr = gl.BlockedLayout([4], [32], [4], [0])
    offs = gl.arange(0, N, L)
    smem = gl.allocate_shared_memory(SMEM_DTYPE, [N], gl.SwizzledSharedLayout(1, 1, 1, [0]))
    async_copy.async_load(smem, inp + offs)
    async_copy.commit_group()
    async_copy.wait_group(0)
    gl.store(out + offs, smem.load(L))


N = 512
inp = torch.arange(N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) + 0.5
out = torch.zeros(N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
kernel[(1, )](inp, out, gl.float16, N)  # fp32 pointer -> fp16 smem: compiles, wrong values
print(out[:8].tolist())

inp = torch.arange(N, device="cuda").to(torch.float16)
out = torch.zeros(N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
kernel[(1, )](inp, out, gl.float32, N)  # fp16 pointer -> fp32 smem
torch.cuda.synchronize()                # RuntimeError: CUDA error: misaligned address
```

```
[0.0, 1.75, 0.0, 1.9375, 0.0, 2.28125, 0.0, 2.34375]
RuntimeError: CUDA error: misaligned address
```

The first kernel should print `[0.5, 1.5, 2.5, ...]`; instead each 8-byte copy moves the raw bytes of two fp32 values into four fp16 slots.

Expected: a compile-time error for both, like `smem.store` gives for a value whose dtype does not match the buffer.

The frontend (`python/triton/experimental/gluon/language/nvidia/ampere/async_copy.py`, and the AMD `cdna4`/`cdna5` versions) only checks the shapes, and `AsyncCopyGlobalToLocalOp::verify` only checks that the destination is mutable. The lowering sizes each copy by the shared memory element type, so a mismatch reads with the wrong stride.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8
